title: Grateful Dead Live at Student Union Ballroom, U. Utah on 1969-04-12
lineage: SBD > MC > C > D > CD > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Analog‑sounding soundboard capture of a loose, experimental 4/12/69 Utah show featuring a smoking The Eleven and a powerful Dark Star, despite hiss, splices and missing sections.
ai_review.review: The recording delivers the warm analog hiss that many Deadheads love, but suffers from noticeable cuts (the Other One is gone, early Dark Star and parts of Lovelight are spliced) and occasional pitch drift. Musically the night shines with a hot The Eleven, an inspired Dark Star, a beautiful Lovelight “shine on me” moment and solid performances of Dew and Friend of Mine, making it a memorable, if slightly imperfect, snapshot of the band’s late‑’60s improvisational spirit.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers rate the show 4–5 stars and praise key performances, while noting consistent recording flaws; weighted combination yields a solid above‑average rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Analog hiss is present and embraced by listeners; there are audible cuts (missing Other One, truncated Dark Star intro, splice in Lovelight) and pitch‑correction issues noted in the early set. Overall listenable but not pristine.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A loose, experimental two‑set show with a curfew‑imposed early set; the band trades jokes (Yellow Dog story) and stretches out jams, delivering strong improvisations despite some missing material.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Noted as agitated by a non‑dancing crowd but still delivering tight interplay with Pigpen; his guitar work remains compelling throughout.
